context.body: Servant presentation and divine delight supply a strong verbal field for the baptism voice.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: God presents a chosen servant, delights in him, and puts his Spirit on him for justice among the nations.
observations.label: God delights in the servant and puts the Spirit on him: action

observations.body: The servant acts without public display, preserves what is bruised, and becomes covenant and light.
observations.label: God delights in the servant and puts the Spirit on him: response

observations.body: my servant · chosen · delight · Spirit · justice
observations.label: Words in Isaiah 42:1–9

payload.posture: Read Isaiah 42:1–9 as voices before the jordan evidence before carrying it into another source.
payload.tension: The Gospel voice is not a verbatim quotation of one verse; royal and servant language may be heard together.
payload.title: God delights in the servant and puts the Spirit on him
